additional_card: Pack 92 duplicates Chapter 2 wording; apply the accepted pack 94 translation.
method: Read both native contact sheets for all 31 cards and compared all 30 draft titles and English subtitles.
Examined individual native images for packs 100, 112, 113 and 114 to disambiguate lettering.
Decoded 46 chapter/title UI strings from the original ELF and checked each indexed source byte hash; no hash mismatches.
Reviewed meaning rather than personal style. No newly named characters, places or organizations occur in translated Japanese titles.
heading_policy: Chapter 1 through Chapter 16 and Final Chapter. Preserve three-star unnumbered cards without inventing a heading.
subtitle_policy: Preserve the existing English wording and case, including Erugo, Genteel Agreement and source punctuation; do not silently modernize the subtitle translation.

uncertainties.issue: Japanese titles do not explicitly mark singular/plural. Current readings are plausible and require no correction.
The Japanese insult covers cowardice and dishonorable conduct. Coward is defensible; full chapter narrative was not audited for a more specific intended epithet.
The final Japanese conjunction leaves an open-ended nuance. Mother and Child is accepted as a natural title.
Erugo is existing English source artwork, preserved as requested; this review does not establish it as a normalized glossary spelling.

limitations: Meaning approval does not certify pixel layout, runtime loading, or all possible chapter-title consumers.
The 23 paired ELF records do not establish headings for the other seven artwork titles.
